newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt bans entry of Israeli businesswoman.
newsitem.headline: Egypt bans entry of Israeli businesswoman.

text.p: Israeli opposition leader Ehud Barak delayed his departure from Cairo airport on Wednesday to take home an Israeli businesswoman who was banned from entering Egypt, airport sources said.
They said Barak, who had talks with President Hosni Mubarak on the Middle East peace process, asked the airport officials to let him take back businesswoman Dvora Ganani.
Ganani was prevented from entering the country on Tuesday because her name was on a black list.
She spent the night at a transit hotel and was going to be sent back to Israel on the first flight out, the sources added. Ganani was not interrogated during her stay, they added.
But in Israel, her son Amos told Israel Radio that police questioned his mother for four hours for unspecified security reasons.
His mother had been living in Cairo for several years arranging Egyptian-Israeli joint ventures in the plastics, agriculture and cosmetics industry, he added.

In April, Egypt put on trial an Israeli texile mechanic charged with spying for Israel's secret service Mossad. The case has further chilled Egyptian-Israeli relations and aroused public suspicion of Israelis working in the country.
